findings.claim: The fold's headline semantic (the twin writer moved to an always-run step in initCommand) has no command-level sensor: every `.agents` assertion calls distributeClaudeSkills directly with explicit roots; no test runs initCommand and reads a path under `.agents/`. Reverting fold 1 (the writer back inside installClaudeHooks, the always-run step deleted) leaves all 549 tests green. Issue mmnto-ai/totem#2899 § Verification names a test that RUNS init verbatim, and charter mmnto-ai/totem#2788 § Done when is command-level too.
findings.counterexample: Enumeration: every `.agents` hit in init.test.ts sits at 3573-3684 inside describe('distributeClaudeSkills …') calling the helper directly; the only other hit (4114+) reads this repo's committed byte-copies. Headless fixtures C (.gemini + GEMINI.md + empty .agents/, no Claude surface) and H (no AI tool at all + .agents/) each wrote four .agents/skills/*/SKILL.md — the only evidence the placement works. Orchestrator RED: with the always-run block deleted (18 lines) the new command-level test failed on `.agents/skills/signoff/SKILL.md: expected false to be true`; restored, it passes.

findings.claim: The new parity installHint names `run totem init from the repository root` as the remedy, and core threads one hint into three branches including the markers-absent WARN (`Restore the managed block via ${install}`), but a plain init PRESERVES a marker-stripped twin, so the remedy is inert in that branch — the class doctor-parity.ts:170-173 says the field exists to prevent ('an inert remedy is worse than none').

findings.claim: Eject's root list is a hand-mirrored literal in two places (`const roots = ['.claude', '.agents']` at 641 and both literal paths in the dirty-tree roster at 1141-1144) while init reads SKILL_TWIN_ROOTS — the fold rebuilds on the root dimension the drift class M1 closed on the name dimension, directly under the docblock (630-633) that says the scrub list is derived so a hand-mirrored list can never orphan. Side effect: SKILL_TWIN_ROOTS has no production consumer (both call sites pass explicit roots), and the changeset advertises it.
findings.counterexample: grep -rn SKILL_TWIN_ROOTS packages/ --include=*.ts → 4 hits, all init.ts (604, 605, 623) and init.test.ts (52, 3574); zero in eject.ts; `grep -n "from './init" eject.ts` → empty.

findings.claim: A fourth stale prose site, inside the guard itself: the comment says never 'via totem init' '(which does not write .agents/skills until slice 2)', and the three `not.toContain('via totem init')` assertions now lock phrasing, not the invariant — the shipped hint DOES recommend init and passes only because its literal is 'run totem init'.

findings.claim: Fold 1's M10 restore of `// eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-require-imports` adds one ESLint warning (net 7 → 8): eslint.config.mjs:70 sets the rule 'off' with no files scope, so the directive can never be used, and the next `eslint --fix` deletes it again — which is how it vanished in the first build.
findings.counterexample: `pnpm --filter @mmnto/cli exec eslint <five touched files>` → `3290:5 warning Unused eslint-disable directive`, ✖ 1 problem (0 errors, 1 warning); package-wide `eslint src/` → 8 problems (0 errors, 8 warnings), 7 before the fold; `lint` script has no --max-warnings.

findings.claim: Shape-grounded, failure not reproduced: the twin probe is an unguarded `fs.existsSync(p) && fs.statSync(p).isDirectory()` inside a command whose body is try/finally with no catch (init.ts:2352-2354), so an EPERM/EACCES/TOCTOU throw there escapes past the summary and the remaining always-run steps, departing from the posture at init.ts:783 (preserve on any IO failure rather than abort init mid-flight).
findings.counterexample: Fault injection by patching fs.statSync did not take (dist imports `node:fs` as a namespace snapshot); the run completed normally. Reachability low; treated as a shape finding.

findings.claim: Coupled surface out of repo: mmnto-ai/totem-strategy:doctrine/parity-manifest.yaml:292-298 (and its packages/strategy-doctrine copy) discloses a MECHANISM GAP — 'totem init writes .claude/skills ONLY … until mmnto-ai/totem#2788 has init write both surfaces' — that becomes false on merge; neither the PR body's 'Not in this PR' nor 'Related' names it as owed. The same read CONFIRMS the fold's contract citation (lines 286-287: byte-equality is the zero-extension case, the detector checks managed-block equality only).

Disclosed noise for the seat to rule: every non-bare init in a repo without `.agents/` now prints the skipped row (before the fold only when Claude was detected; never at caba03c6); every eject in such a repo prints four `.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md (not found)` skipped rows and four `??` dirty-sense rows. Also: `initCommand({yes:true, bare:true})` writes no twins and prints no row, and the docs sentence ('whichever AI tools were detected') does not carve out --bare.

findings.claim: An intentional preserve is announced as an error: a marker-less twin yields `[Totem Error] Skill twin scaffolding failed for …: … preserving.` above 'Init complete' — symmetric with the pre-existing .claude path ('Hook scaffolding failed'), so not a regression, but the changeset's 'a marker-less twin is preserved' reads as a quiet no-op while the user sees a red line. Latent coupling: the always-run step prints a row only when summaryActionOverride is set, whereas the installer loop prints created/merged rows with a default label; today twinLabel covers both so nothing is dropped.
